overall: Los Angeles is experiencing a classic June Gloom pattern on 2026-06-25, with overnight and early morning temperatures locked in an unusually flat 62–63°F range since midnight — essentially zero warming velocity through 06:45 ET. The marine layer and patchy fog (expected to persist until around 11am per NWS) are suppressing any early-morning heating, with onshore southwest flow (3–10 mph) reinforcing the cool, humid pattern. The active Beach Hazards Statement for strong south-southwest swell confirms a robust marine influence along the Southern California coast today.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models show moderate agreement in a 67–70°F range: NBM is the coolest at 67.0°F, ECMWF sits at 68.2°F, and HRRR is the most aggressive at 70.3°F — a spread of ~3.3°F. The NWS official forecast of 69°F falls in the middle of this envelope, lending reasonable confidence. The current running max of just 63.0°F means all models are projecting substantial afternoon warming (4–7°F above current max), which is plausible if the marine layer clears by midday, but the mostly-cloudy afternoon sky and continued onshore flow tilt risk slightly to the downside.
max_temp_prediction: With the fog expected to clear around 11am, some afternoon sun through partly-to-mostly cloudy skies should allow warming into the upper 60s. The NWP model consensus (ECMWF 68.2°F, NBM 67.0°F, HRRR 70.3°F) and NWS 69°F forecast anchor the likely high in the 67–70°F range. Given the persistent marine layer, muted current warming trend (velocity near 0°F/hr at 06:45 ET), and mostly cloudy afternoon sky, the downside risk to the HRRR's 70.3°F is real; the central estimate aligns closer to ECMWF/NWS around 68–69°F. Confidence is moderate — the key variable is how thoroughly the fog and low clouds clear by early afternoon.
